canal_p23_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_001.text: On the fifty-fourth morning the canal seemed almost offensively ordinary. A woman shook her bed quilt from a window, the bakery burned one tray, and a pilot complained that the new gate made no allowance for his late arrival. Luo held him to the posted interval. Yue stood beside the movement board during a final accepted receiving check, watching actual boats match actual entries. Her stage-four practice had not changed the water's opinion of schedules. The repaired cap made the same little sound under each passing bow, indifferent to how much its construction had worried them.

canal_p23_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_002.text: The operating book through yesterday showed thirty-three copper actually received and thirty-two actually paid. Its thirty-six-copper two-month budget was a cap, not proof that all thirty-six had been collected or spent. Pei kept the remaining accepted service costs beside the current passages expected before closure. The one-copper balance stayed in its own account. No future forecast filled a gap automatically. Han inspected the current figures because they affected his loan's eligible receipts, then remarked that the canal seemed determined to preserve his skill at waiting. Luo told him waiting was among his least-developed skills.

canal_p23_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_003.text: Yue checked a prepaid token against its earlier receipt instead of counting its present boat as new coin. The pilot noticed and accused her of forgetting his current passage. She showed him the separate use mark. Both his payment and service remained visible, without producing a second copper for the public box. He read the corrected line and nodded grudgingly. At the next boat he helped another customer find the posted interval. Yue smiled at the unexpected usefulness, then caught herself before awarding him permanent character improvement for one sensible minute.

canal_p23_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_004.text: The young keeper completed the current morning round and opened her market stall before the first customers arrived. Luo did not repeat the whole route afterward. She checked only the actual question the girl had reported: a lower marker partly hidden by a basket. The basket owner moved it. Their future short-round fee would be divided according to the accepted work, with no old household row waiting behind it. Yue watched the principal keeper return to her own breakfast. A service plan that allowed breakfast felt more convincing than one depending on universal readiness.

canal_p23_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_005.text: The winter assistant practiced the final folder retrieval inside her current paid closing-week interval. Pei asked for the quarry finding, the lease receiving condition, and the route-office estimate acknowledgment in an order different from yesterday's. The woman found all three. She had labeled the shelf broadly enough that memory was not its only key. The limited winter grant would begin after closure, two actual copper per month for two months. Pei looked at the empty place beside her own chair. "Do not become indispensable," she said. The assistant replied that this depended partly on Pei permitting ordinary labels.

canal_p23_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_006.text: Han's family letters returned from the private conservator before noon. Some lines remained broken where water had lifted ink from the sheet; the selected drying treatment could preserve what survived, not invent the missing words. Han paid the final accepted private price from current business funds and kept the receipt out of the loan account. His wife placed the recovered pieces on their own table. Yue heard they had arrived but did not enter without invitation. The chest had been a private grief before the storm made everybody curious about its contents.

canal_p23_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_007.text: The invitation came in Han's own words that afternoon. He wanted Yue and Tian to see one letter his mother had written after the founding flood, not every family page. His note mentioned timber, his father's stubborn leg, and a neighbor who fed everyone burnt millet. The letter was not the original loan agreement. Missing words would stay missing; any remembered phrase would be identified as memory. Yue appreciated the limit before accepting the possible visit. He was offering a family page on purpose, rather than waiting for somebody to turn it into another source for the public account.

canal_p23_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_008.text: Bao's sister said he had spent the morning teaching a young carpenter to mark a small bracket on waste wood. The sitting lesson stayed brief and did not require loaded grip. His own wrist still weakened when he closed his hand, though ordinary motion had improved. He had declined the private planing job and not yet accepted the priced drawing interval offered for next week. Yue knew he would resent being described as wise for obeying pain. She asked whether he wanted company after her public check. He said yes and immediately warned that he would criticize her posture.

canal_p23_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_009.text: Tian's actual sail fitting was due tomorrow afternoon. The customer had brought the intended ordinary test arrangement to the permitted work place, where the loft observer would inspect it before loading. The real cloth differed from the sample in age and stretch. Tian checked the finished corner under her own work agreement, stopping when a fold showed strain she had not liked on the trestle. She unpicked a short run and resewed it before the fitting. Yue wanted to say the sample had passed. Tian held up the changed cloth. "This one did not hear about that."

canal_p23_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_010.text: Her mother brought food and watched the repair without offering to make Tian remain in town. They discussed the trial's six weeks, paid terms, lodging, and ordinary return passage again. Passing would leave Tian free to accept or refuse. It would begin a fortnight after canal closure, the seventieth day on the current count, leaving time for her existing local orders and the agreed journey downriver. Yue checked that she would not be around to escort her. Tian said she knew. A friendship could support a departure without arranging to own the road beside it.

canal_p23_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_011.text: Luo practiced tending the plant once more under Tian's instruction. She tested the soil with an ordinary finger, gave the small measured drink, and placed the pot away from the stove's hottest draft. Tian approved the effort. The keeper looked absurdly pleased and asked whether the plant had a name. "You may not name it Bao," Tian said. Luo protested that this left her with fewer choices than the apparatus screws. Yue laughed until the young keeper came in asking where the gate key had been left. It was on its named hook, which disappointed everyone hoping for another joke.

canal_p23_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_012.text: The old check worker read the current winter task board and found an upstream employer's actual two-hour rope inspection offer. Its rate and travel interval were stated; he would have to ask the employer whether his ordinary competence fitted. The notice did not appoint him. He copied the contact and went to inquire. The assistant placed the unanswered status beside it. Yue was glad to see a real possibility reach the right person, even before it became work. The washerwoman pointed out that the board had finally acquired enough plain words to survive market gossip.

canal_p23_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_013.text: The cabinet maker delivered his table and completed the private storage rack inside the shed from his own priced stock. The sound common strip remained clear, and the damaged return edge stayed closed. His apprentice brought the agreed notice acknowledgment to the office during an ordinary errand. No public purchase had bought the rack. The landlord's next-month rent reduction remained in their private amendment. Yue saw how the corrected route now occupied less daily conversation than it had caused on discovery. That was useful progress: people could return to tables without pretending the public line had vanished again.

canal_p23_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_014.text: The gardener had begun sorting seed varieties for spring instead of comparing every visitor's sympathy. The four-copper quarry contribution and earlier hardship gift had their own receiving notes; his household chose how to use the actual money. The reed family planned a smaller sale from surviving stock. The stall owner had priced another batch with current fuel costs. Their food grain stayed household provision, not business stock or a compensation waiver. Yue could hear these different futures from the landing, where people argued over sacks and weather. The loss hearing had not made them speak with one voice.

canal_p23_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_015.text: Ren's appointment still stood on the fifty-ninth morning. Yue's three-copper ordinary fare was booked and paid; two copper for beds and two for food waited in her personal road purse. The optional kiln connection remained another copper only if selected. Her cumulative ordinary canal pay was twenty, with four still to be earned through actual final work. She checked the remaining intervals against the accepted full orchard review. The proposed journey no longer depended on obtaining one more kind letter. It depended on leaving when she had said she would leave.

canal_p23_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_016.text: At the flour-store room Yue practiced the small breathing routine she already knew. She made no new pair or realm, and sent no command into the disconnected apparatus. A steady ordinary posture let her notice where fatigue made concentration brittle. She stopped before the practice became an excuse to postpone supper. From outside came Tian's short frustrated exclamation at a thread knot. Yue nearly called out advice and then remembered how badly she sewed. She went to fetch her own bowl instead. Her training remained hers, useful in limits it did not need to exaggerate.

canal_p23_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_017.text: The public route authority acknowledged the separate repair estimate for the old step and damaged return. It would enter the ordinary works review after the current closure; no date or money had yet been approved. The visible barriers and safe alternatives remained current decisions. Luo read the acknowledgment and sighed, then filed it where the winter assistant could find it. She had stopped asking Yue to stay until approval. The officer knew the hazard. The town had an actual receiver. Further work would need the next authorized people and funds, rather than one exhausted apprentice delaying a different promise.

canal_p23_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_018.text: The final charter review brought four households' continuing objections. Two feared voluntary work would leave future banks unattended; one disputed the ordinary tariff; one wanted debt payments suspended until all storm losses were restored. The chair accepted the comments without reopening completed money counts. The twenty-eight current household responses would be counted at closure after the posted interval. Dissent would remain with the approved record and would not remove ordinary lawful water access. Yue delivered the fourth reply to Pei. The clerk asked her to make its smallest handwriting legible without improving its opinion.

canal_p23_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_019.text: By evening the fifty-fourth day had finished its actual public checks. Yue could spend one personal interval before tomorrow's closing work resumed. Tian had invited her to the sail fitting if she wished. Bao wanted company during a short sitting lesson and a possible recovery review. Han had offered to read one retained family letter with his wife's agreement. These were relationships, not extra duties inserted into the labor book. The invitations might deepen what she remembered about leaving. None would add charged fuel, a realm, or authority over the person's future who had offered it.

canal_p23_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_020.text: Tian asked Yue to arrive at the fitting as a friend rather than a public witness expected to pronounce the sail safe. The actual customer and qualified loft observer would inspect the ordinary arrangement and determine the result. Yue could hold light cloth only if asked in an unloaded stage. She accepted the distinction with a grin. "I will try to look less official." Tian said removing the measuring rule from her sleeve would help. Yue had already returned it to the commission store, but confessed that she still felt its shape there when somebody asked a difficult question.

canal_p23_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_021.text: Bao's invitation included a chair, tea, and the right to disagree with his account of carpentry. The clinician would review his continuing weakness at the private appointment if symptoms still warranted it. Yue had no power to certify recovery. His sister wrote the brief visiting interval on the note because he would otherwise pretend time passed differently when he enjoyed an argument. Yue read the note and laughed. She thought of the stool at the funeral landing and the old boatwoman's seated testimony. A chair had become one of the commission's most persistent useful ideas without belonging to its apparatus.

canal_p23_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_022.text: Han's letter viewing would concern the one page he chose to share. The missing lines would remain missing. His wife would not answer for his permission, and neither Yue nor Tian would turn private phrases into loan evidence simply because the public account had finally become clear. He said this almost sternly in his note, as if he expected admiration to trespass more readily than suspicion. Yue appreciated the precaution. She had spent weeks asking him to distinguish his family's story from its valid claim. Now he was inviting her into the story on purpose.

canal_p23_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_023.text: Luo looked at Yue's three invitations and said she ought to choose whichever contained the best food. Tian had apparently mentioned buns, Bao's sister had promised tea, and Han's wife made excellent pickles. Yue asked whether the keeper applied this method to all decisions. "Only the ones after work," Luo replied. She packed tomorrow's ordinary round bag and left the young keeper's share where it belonged. Their future work would continue after Yue went. The keeper did not mention it as a reason to take any of the invitations away from her.

canal_p23_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_024.text: A messenger from the upstream employer returned the check worker's inquiry. The rope inspection was within his demonstrated ordinary skill, and the actual two-hour appointment was offered at the posted price including its stated local route. He accepted after checking the time. It was one job, not a winter salary. The assistant updated its status and end time. Yue had watched enough empty promises travel through the town to appreciate this modest complete exchange. When the worker passed the lock, he held the note up without stopping. He was already thinking about the rope he would inspect.

canal_p23_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_025.text: The fifteen-year-old niece who had helped recover Qiao Lan's personal account brought a short reply from her aunt. The repaired name was now in the received copy, and the aunt approved the chosen words about the old work. She had no wish to attend another meeting. Yue accepted the reply and kept her absent voice from acquiring a new duty at closure. The niece wanted to know whether the old song had been completed. Yue said its missing lines remained missing. The girl hummed the surviving part anyway while leaving, which seemed a better use of it than inventing certainty.

canal_p23_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_026.text: The night before the fitting stayed dry. Tian rolled the sail into its private cover, Bao put the waste-wood drawing board aside, and Han laid the chosen letter on his own table. Yue finished her ordinary closing notes before considering where to spend the personal interval. Ren's accepted appointment sat beside her road purse. She had finally arranged one return honestly; tomorrow she would be choosing a farewell she could actually attend. The canal's low sound reached through the window. It no longer resembled a question demanding that she answer every part of it.

canal_p23_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_027.text: On the fifty-fifth morning Yue completed the appointed early receiving check with the young keeper. Two small cargo receipts and their actual passages brought the ordinary operating gross toward its final count; they were not the personal passage fare already paid elsewhere. The clerk would settle costs at closure. Yue put the source book back on its public shelf. The rest of the morning was available for her chosen personal interval and the practical preparations around it. She did not make the labor account purchase another hour merely because she remained near the lock.

canal_p23_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_028.text: At midday the sail customer and loft observer arrived at the private work place. Bao's sister sent word that his short seated interval still suited him. Han's wife opened their own room for the chosen letter reading. Yue saw all three invitations resting on real people who had prepared something, and knew she could not attend them all at once. The others would continue in their ordinary lives if she went elsewhere. She tightened her coat's mended sleeve and thanked Luo for the kettle water. It was time to choose a conversation rather than a danger.

canal_p23_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_029.text: Yue left the keeper's room with no commission tool in her sleeve. One way led to Tian's practical fitting; another to Bao's chair and ordinary recovery; the third to Han's private family page. These choices would not change the accepted orchard date or the final public work still due. They would change what she heard before departure and how she said goodbye. She chose the invitation she wished to accept first, allowing friendship to ask a genuine question without disguising it as another task someone had assigned her.

choices.text: Attend Tian Min's actual sail fitting as her friend.
Visit Bao Jun for his sitting lesson and recovery review.
Hear the private family page Han Shou chooses to share.

canal_p23_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_030.text: Tian stood beside the actual sail while the loft observer inspected the intended ordinary fitting arrangement. The boat owner kept his vessel secured on its checked moorings; nobody treated a gust as permission to test a higher load. Yue stayed with Tian's mother on the sound work platform. The observer asked who had repaired the corner. Tian answered herself and showed the new double seam. She did not display the sample report first as if its good result could speak for different cloth. The observer examined the real work closely, then agreed to the named test sequence.

canal_p23_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_031.text: The first ordinary tension settled the cloth and made one small fold appear where the old sail had stretched unevenly. Tian asked to unload before the fold could pull against the stitching. The owner groaned; he wanted to leave before evening. The observer agreed with the stop and let the arrangement return safely to its unloaded condition. Yue heard Tian's mother inhale, then say nothing. Tian marked the new fold with chalk. The problem was in the fitted cloth's shape, not proof that her entire seam was useless. She could correct it within the agreed work price.

canal_p23_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_032.text: While Tian adjusted the fold, the owner asked whether the public apprentice could help hold the heavy loaded corner. Yue said the observer's arrangement already had its qualified handlers; she would not enter under tension merely because she was present. He looked irritated. Tian told him to stop collecting extra hands before asking what they would do. Yue stood with the mother and held only the loose light offcut Tian offered for marking. Her trained arms could remain unused. The sail would pass or fail under its actual ordinary work conditions, which made the result Tian's rather than borrowed spectacle.

canal_p23_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_033.text: The second fitting used the corrected fold after the observer checked it. The intended ordinary tension held through the full observation interval without the earlier creeping corner. The boat owner examined both faces of the seam before accepting the repair. The observer recorded the result and the changed step, not a claim that the sail could withstand any storm. Tian read the report with fingers that shook slightly despite having sewn steadily. Yue saw her mother reach toward her, stop, and wait. Tian gave the paper to her voluntarily. The older woman's smile appeared slowly and then refused to leave.

canal_p23_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_034.text: The owner paid the remaining accepted private order price on receiving the sail. That completed Tian's local transaction; the loft trial was still a different offer. The observer repeated its six paid weeks, named lodging, resident forewoman, and ordinary return travel. It would begin a fortnight after canal closure if Tian accepted. He gave her until tomorrow's agreed interval to answer. Tian looked at Yue for neither permission nor courage. She asked her mother whether they could walk home together before deciding. Yue was glad to hear a real pause requested while success was still making everyone impatient.

canal_p23_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_035.text: They bought warm buns from their own money and ate by the permitted landing. Tian's mother said she feared the distance but could now imagine the forewoman as a person rather than a line in an offer. Tian said she wanted to learn the larger sail work, not leave town because it had treated her badly. Both statements mattered. Yue spoke of the orchard road only when asked. She had an accepted date and still dreaded the answers awaiting her. Tian laughed softly. "Then courage has a very poor sense of timing." Yue agreed without offering to cure the defect.

canal_p23_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_036.text: At home Tian read the offer once more, including the ordinary return fare clarification. She chose to accept the six-week paid trial beginning on the seventieth day, with the confirmed practical result attached. Her mother did not sign for her. Tian sent the actual acceptance through her private message arrangement before the deadline. Yue witnessed the decision as an invited friend, not a public authorizing officer. The next fortnight would hold her remaining local orders and travel preparation. She did not promise never to return, or to return unchanged. She had accepted work she wanted to attempt.

canal_p23_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_037.text: Luo received the plant-care request in its final small form. Tian would leave the pot with her for the six-week trial and collect it afterward if it remained hers to bring home. The keeper could contact Tian's mother if it needed a different window. It was not a gift of the plant or an appointment to supervise the seamstress's life. Luo protested that everybody now gave her instructions as though she were a child. Tian said the chilies she had watered made excellent references. Yue laughed until the keeper turned the watering cup toward her threateningly.

canal_p23_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_038.text: Tian gave Yue a short scrap of thread cut from waste, the same ordinary personal keepsake she had already offered. She asked Yue to remember the stopped first fitting as well as the accepted second one. Yue said she would probably remember the owner trying to recruit her arms. They agreed that this was less poetic and more accurate. The larger sail rolled into its private cover. The customer took it away under his own ordinary transport arrangement. Nothing about the successful trial left a public apparatus or a new cultivation mark in Yue's pack.

canal_p23_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_039.text: When Yue left, Tian and her mother were listing food for the downriver journey. The loft's acceptance reply still had to arrive, but Tian's own decision and successful assessment were real. She called Yue back from the doorway to say goodbye before tomorrow's public closing grew crowded. They embraced awkwardly around the sewing basket, then laughed at the handles between them. Yue promised no shared road she had not booked. Tian said, "Come somewhere because you want to see me, one day." Yue answered that she wanted that, and would ask for an actual date when she could.

canal_p23_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_040.text: Bao had arranged two chairs and then pretended he had not done so. Yue sat in the less comfortable one because he had left his support cloth on the other. His young pupil stood beside a waste-wood bracket marked with three lines. One was right, one was careless, and one was evidence of a promising imagination unsuited to joinery. Bao described the difference without taking the tool himself. Yue thought he seemed calmer until the pupil called the wrong line better looking. Bao shut his eyes. "I have raised a poet," he said, with genuine dismay.

canal_p23_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_041.text: The sitting lesson stayed inside the brief interval Bao had chosen. The pupil repeated the mark under his spoken instruction, checked the reference face, and showed the sound result. Bao let him explain it back rather than providing the answer twice. When the youngster left, the carpenter admitted that teaching had made him more tired than he expected. Yue offered to go. He asked her to stay for tea while his sister prepared the ordinary clinic visit. The request contained no hidden work. She sat, grateful not to be given another urgent task as the price of remaining near him.

canal_p23_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_042.text: The clinician reviewed the wrist's actual improvement that afternoon. Bao could move it more freely and had less tenderness, but firm grip still weakened and brought pain. Loaded carpentry remained barred. Short light movement and seated drawing review could continue within the stated limit, with another review if progress stalled. He paid the private visit from his household funds; no public relief promise covered it. Yue heard only the work permission Bao invited her to hear. His sister kept the private examination details. The body's calendar had not changed because the commission was about to close.

canal_p23_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_043.text: On the walk home Bao stopped before the repaired path turn and looked at the stones. He said the mason had finished the work as well as he would have. Yue waited for the insult he usually added. None came. He was not pleased to have been injured, and he still wanted the private planing job his hand could not accept. But the repair existed without requiring him to prove he was the only useful carpenter. Yue said the young pupil would remember his lesson. Bao replied that this was probably why he ought to make fewer jokes about poetry.

canal_p23_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_044.text: The private drawing review offered for next week was priced at half a copper for its seated interval, with no loaded tool use. Bao compared it with the clinician's current permission and accepted only that task, not an attached promise to finish the carpentry afterward. The employer replied in writing. His sister put the sheet beside the household accounts and asked him to say if pain changed. Bao agreed, looking embarrassed by how ordinary the job sounded. Yue told him a drawing could prevent a bad loaded cut. He said he knew; knowing and liking his limits were different occupations.

canal_p23_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_045.text: They drank tea in the yard while the light moved off the door. Bao asked whether Yue feared going back to people she had once impressed. She admitted that the orchard visit might reveal uneven results and failures she had not understood before. He nodded at his wrist. "Perhaps you will be allowed to look before you fix." She smiled at the advice. It was harder to take from a carpenter who had resisted the same order thoroughly. He saw the thought and laughed. His sister appeared with water before either could make the conversation wise enough to become tedious.

canal_p23_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_046.text: Yue told him the fifty-ninth appointment was actually accepted and her ordinary journey paid and provisioned. Any physical return still owed remained unfinished until arrival. Bao said he would remember the distinction when she tried to send a beautifully written apology instead of turning up. She accepted the teasing. He asked her to leave the public drawing notes with Luo, which she had already planned. His own private rule was back at home. They would meet at closure for the brief seated interval if his body still allowed it; otherwise his actual receiving copy would be enough.

canal_p23_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_047.text: Bao's sister asked Yue to help fold the extra chair before leaving. Bao started to rise, then sat again while the two women completed the light ordinary household task. He made no attempt to claim it was unfair to his reputation. The chair folded badly until Yue found its simple catch. His sister said it behaved like every man in the family: complicated only when not listened to. Bao objected from the doorway and received no answer. Yue left laughing, with no sense that the clinic's continued restriction had robbed the afternoon of a satisfying ending.

canal_p23_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_048.text: At the gate Bao called her back to return the personal note she had left beside his cup. It carried the ordinary travel dates and nothing he needed to retain. He had copied the closure interval onto his own small calendar with his sound hand. Yue thanked him. She thought of how often records became proof that a person could keep another person nearby. This one marked when each would be elsewhere. Bao said she should not turn it into a philosophical problem. She said he had turned it into a crooked date. They parted with both accusations unanswered.

canal_p23_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_049.text: The visit ended before Bao's wrist grew tired. He kept his clinic permission, accepted short drawing appointment, and actual paid work records at home. Yue kept only her personal travel leaf. The carpenter had not recovered full strength or given a loaded final demonstration. He had found a way to teach and accept a limited private task while waiting. At the lock Luo asked how he was. Yue gave the work restriction he had permitted her to share and said the tea was terrible. The keeper looked affronted on behalf of the entire district's kettles.

canal_p23_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_050.text: Han set the chosen family letter on a clean private board and asked Yue to sit where the light caught its surviving lines. His wife sat beside him. Tian had another preparation interval elsewhere and had not been assumed into the invitation merely because her name had appeared earlier. Han showed the wet damage without apology for the paper's appearance. The conservator's selected treatment had preserved what remained; blank places had no trustworthy restored words. Yue put away her copying pen. She had come to hear a page he wanted to share, not take another source for the public hearing.

canal_p23_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_051.text: His mother had written after the founding flood that the timber cutters arrived hungry and angry at one another. Han read the next line about burnt millet, then laughed unexpectedly. His father had insisted the cook was improving every day while secretly feeding the worst crust to a dog. Han had been twenty-two, old enough to be injured and foolish, not a child carried through that winter. The supported leg in the letter matched his actual adult memory. Yue heard the story without mistaking its warmth for a new term allowing labor from today's descendants.

canal_p23_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_052.text: At a missing passage Han stopped. His wife remembered his mother complaining about a neighbor's borrowed bowl, but they could not place the words exactly. They left the blank alone. Han touched the edge of the private board, careful not to rub the damaged sheet. "I used to think the missing part must explain us better." Yue asked what he meant. He said every family had a version in which its fear justified what it later demanded. The public original had answered the debt. This page might never answer all the fears he had placed around it.

canal_p23_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_053.text: His wife said the smaller private loading operation could still keep their current crew if the accepted lease began and winter trade stayed near its cautious estimate. They would review real receipts, not inherit the old sale's imagined profit. Han looked relieved by the ordinary possibility and ashamed of needing it. Yue did not promise his shop would prosper. She asked what part of the work he still enjoyed. He answered slowly: boats arriving with goods someone elsewhere had made. It was a modest pleasure for a man who had nearly sold the people living beside their route.

canal_p23_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_054.text: He brought out the forty-eight refund receipt only to put it away in its completed private file. The released security had returned his listed crane, platform, and chest to unencumbered custody under that deposit agreement. The valid remaining public loan stayed separate at fifty-six. Yue did not let the scene turn into another audit. Han knew the account now. His wife brought pickles, and for several minutes they talked about which barrel had made the temporary storage yard smell of old plums. Han said he would never again accept generosity from fruit without inspecting its contract.

canal_p23_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_055.text: Tian arrived later, after her own ordinary preparation allowed it, and Han repeated the surviving letter lines he had agreed to share. She asked about the burnt millet cook. He gave the actual remembered name, which she recognized as her great-aunt's cousin. Neither had expected the connection. Tian wanted to ask her mother about it before repeating the story publicly. Han approved that private inquiry but asked her not to copy the damaged letter. She accepted. A family page could make two people laugh together without becoming common property because the laugh seemed useful.

canal_p23_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_056.text: The conversation turned to Tian's possible winter trial. Han wanted to congratulate her before knowing the fitting result and stopped himself. She said success would matter, then her choice would matter. His wife asked about lodging. Tian explained the named forewoman and clarified return passage. Yue saw the familiar concern lose some of its sharpness when it received a real answer. Han said he had left home once at her age to learn a trade, returned early, and concealed the reason for years. His wife looked at him. "You disliked the food," she said. He admitted this with wounded dignity.

canal_p23_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_057.text: Tian left in time for her actual sail task, taking no copied family page. At Han's request, Yue helped replace the chosen letter in its dry cover. The recovered paper had not changed the public finding or the loan term. It had changed the ease with which a former adversary could hear him laugh. She thanked both spouses for inviting her. Han said he hoped the orchard road treated her gently. Yue said the people at its end would be entitled to ask difficult questions. His wife replied that gentle roads did not always lead to gentle tables.

canal_p23_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_058.text: At the door Han asked whether she would tell the next town that he had tried to sell a canal. Yue said the public record was clear and available; she did not need to carry his private humiliation as an entertaining story. He looked relieved and then troubled. He had wanted silence as much as fairness. Yue added that if the record mattered to a real question, she would describe it accurately. He nodded. They had become capable of parting without either affection or hostility deciding whose facts could be mentioned. His wife opened the door into cold afternoon light.

canal_p23_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_059.text: Yue returned to the lock with no family letter in her pack. Han retained his private page, valid claim, completed refund, and smaller uncertain business. Tian retained her own practical assessment and winter decision. Yue retained the afternoon's laughter, which was not a source needing a numbered shelf. Luo asked whether the pickles had been as good as expected. Yue said better. The keeper declared the choice justified and went back to her round. Beyond the shed ordinary water slid beneath the repaired cap, offering nobody a grander title for having learned to listen beside it.

canal_p23_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_060.text: Tian's real sail fitting completed on the fifty-fifth afternoon under the customer and qualified observer's ordinary arrangement. The first creeping fold had been unloaded and corrected; the second fitting held through the intended interval. The customer accepted the repair and paid the remaining private price. The successful result qualified the actual assessment, not every future storm. Yue heard the details directly if present, or from Tian's chosen report afterward. The seamstress said the most important moment had been asking to stop while the owner wanted speed. Her mother looked proud and tried unsuccessfully to hide it.

canal_p23_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_061.text: Tian chose the six-week paid loft trial after reading the clarified lodging and ordinary return travel. It would begin a fortnight after canal closure, on the seventieth day. The loft's authorized observer received her signed acceptance and confirmed its terms on the employer's form. Her next fortnight could hold her current local orders and actual private travel preparation. She would not accompany Yue to the forest or owe the canal another household work season because she left. Luo received the plant for its stated six weeks, with Tian's mother the ordinary alternate if another window became necessary.

canal_p23_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_062.text: Bao's ordinary clinic review still barred loaded carpentry and painful grip. Improved light movement allowed brief seated drawing work under the continuing limit. He accepted the priced half-copper private drawing review for next week, with no hidden promise to finish the loaded job. His own household paid the clinical review; the public work record carried only the necessary restriction he approved. At closure he could attend a brief seated handover if comfortable. Otherwise the accepted copy and actual alternate worker's completed adjustment would be enough. Nobody demanded another demonstration from the injured wrist.

canal_p23_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_063.text: Han's chosen private letter remained with him, its missing lines missing. The conservator's actual private work and paid price belonged outside the public loan. Yue had either heard its surviving words at his invitation or understood that a viewing had taken place without her. It did not add a term to the original contract. His smaller business and accepted gear lease remained uncertain enough to need current receipts. His wife planned the private store's winter hours. The town's corrected public record and this private household could continue without requiring every future visitor to choose which one deserved sympathy.

canal_p23_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_064.text: At the office Pei counted thirty-five operating copper actually received by the end of the fifty-fifth day. Thirty-three had been paid for current accepted service and official dispatches so far, with one final service copper due at closure. The two-copper present balance was therefore not wholly spare. Once that actual cost was paid, one would remain. The original thirty-six budget allowed up to that amount; its unused authorization was not another purse. The separate one-copper wrong-cart material reimbursement already sat in the maintenance account, ready to join the real remaining operating balance after closure.

canal_p23_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_065.text: Yue finished the last pre-closure observation record during her named ordinary hours. Only the final receiving and closure interval remained before the cumulative twenty-four wage total became wholly earned. Twenty had already been paid, including earlier portions used for ordinary food; the last four would be paid after completion. Her personal fare and journey provisions stayed apart from the public accounts. She saw the difference between planning to leave and making a day whose work could actually end. The office folder no longer needed her handwriting to explain where any of its source pages belonged.

canal_p23_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_066.text: The young keeper checked the disconnected frame's cover and the marked stone box during her current appointed round. The meter sheets preserved the selected balances and two hundred forty-four conservative floor, with no new draw since the accepted earlier test. The commissioned objects stayed here. Jiang's work had ended; future powered operation still required a funded qualified appointment and rated measured conditions. Luo watched only the actual receiving check instead of requesting a little pulse for comfort. Yue thanked them both. The girl's correct reply came quickly enough to sound bored, which was a welcome kind of competence.

canal_p23_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_067.text: The household representatives' final responses reached the clerk before the evening deadline. Twenty-four supported the amended charter for closure approval; four retained their stated objections. The responses were actual current household choices, with accepted written replies included, not a claim that every resident had become enthusiastic. Pei set the dissenting comments beside the approval count. Their lawful ordinary water access would remain under the same posted rules. Tian read the voluntary-work clause once more and smiled at its plainness. A seamstress could leave for paid work without leaving a borrowed family back standing at the gate.

canal_p23_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_068.text: The gardener asked the chair to keep future maintenance notices visible early enough for workers to plan planting and other jobs. The chair accepted that practical instruction inside the actual notice process. It promised no new unpriced labor. The reed family asked the warning contact to follow their seasonal departure rather than treating an empty shelter as a receiver. The stall's nephew wanted his early purchasing interval preserved. Yue saw the rota receive three ordinary corrections and remain usable. The charter did not freeze it into a monument; it gave its changes a place to be heard without inventing inheritance.

canal_p23_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_069.text: Han signed receipt of the final debt clause and practical property comparison. The valid fifty-six remained under eligible actual receipts, with four-copper installments requiring fourteen payable months rather than fourteen guaranteed calendar ones. The first future review would follow actual post-closure operating results. His four-copper gear lease had a defined monthly service and reduced crane movement clear of the wall. The completed forty-eight refund stayed complete. He looked at the clause beside the old sale notice and asked if the notice could come down. Luo said yes after final approval, which left him one more night to endure it.

canal_p23_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_070.text: The quarry permit finding and two-copper penalty reference went to the actual regular authority. Its nine-copper household contribution remained in separate four-three-two receipts. The private ten-copper hardship gift and twelve food sacks stayed where their receiving records placed them. Current households kept their chosen claims and accounts under the scoped agreements; no last sentence secretly bought their silence. Yue tied the folder and let the new assistant find it without prompting. She did. The public record was now something another person could use, not a test that required its author's presence at every future question.

canal_p23_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_071.text: The common return's damaged edge and old boarding step remained closed with their safe alternatives shown. The separate route-office estimate had a receiving number and no fabricated approval date. Private platforms and the workboat had moved under their actual owners' arrangements. The tenant's private shed and rent amendment did not become public property through inspection. Yue checked the current notices from their sound approaches one last time. Tomorrow's handover would transfer the copies, not pretend the closed ground had healed because a commission wanted a neat ending. Luo seemed satisfied that the barriers were still ugly enough to be noticed.

canal_p23_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_072.text: Ren's accepted fifty-ninth morning and full review interval stayed fixed. Yue would leave after the fifty-sixth closure and travel ordinarily through the fifty-seventh and fifty-eighth days. Three personal copper had paid the fare; four remained held for food and beds. The optional west-kiln connection cost one more only if chosen. Any physical orchard return still owed under the retained arrangement awaited actual arrival in the next book. Other arrangements kept their different real duties. Yue laid the papers inside her habitual pack and took no public source record or charged store from its shelf.

canal_p23_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_073.text: Tian asked Yue to help carry the plant to Luo's window, an ordinary light task offered between friends. They put the pot where the keeper had actually practiced tending it. Its roots did not know why one young woman was leaving earlier and another later. Luo told them the geese would be kept away if they were sensible enough to accept her authority. Tian said the plant could report any failure to her mother. Yue laughed and wondered how a little leaf had become the one living object in town with more carefully defined representation than most trustees.

canal_p23_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_074.text: Bao came for a brief supper before going home to rest. He saw the plant on the window sill and accused Luo of choosing its care because it would not criticize her carpentry. The keeper answered that criticism had already filled her house to its rated capacity. He sat in the chair placed for him and ate with his sound hand. His sister would collect him after the accepted interval. Yue asked about the younger carpenter's mark. Bao admitted it had improved. He said this as reluctantly as Han had admitted the common bed could not be sold.

canal_p23_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_075.text: Han's wife joined them for a short meal after her private store closed. Han did not come; he wanted to be home with the returned letters and said so plainly. Nobody treated the absence as evidence of renewed hostility. The wife brought pickles she had chosen to share and asked for no public speech afterward. Pei arrived late with the final response count, set it aside, and accepted tea. The assistant stayed only until her private household expected her. The room filled and emptied according to real invitations rather than a demand that the whole cast witness the apprentice's departure.

canal_p23_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_076.text: After supper Luo handed Yue the washed bowl she had used at the keeper's hearth. It belonged to the room and would remain for the next lodger. Yue put it on the shelf herself. Her own tablet, clothes, food bag, and travel papers fitted her pack; survey pegs and reference rules had returned to their actual stores. The personal travel roll Tian had sold her could hold her ordinary things without importing commission equipment. She checked the mended coat, then stopped checking. An honest departure needed preparation, and it also needed an hour in which no new problem was invented.

canal_p23_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_077.text: The old sale notice shivered in the last wind of the fifty-fifth evening. Yue read its unsupported household clause once more and looked toward Tian's darkened workroom. The current charter, paid appointments, accepted tests, private refund, and scoped hearing had changed real decisions since that first morning. They had not repaired every loss or guaranteed the coming winter. A boat bell sounded at its ordinary permitted arrival. Luo answered from the lock, using the agreed words. Yue let the sound finish without running outside. Somebody appointed was already there.

canal_p23_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p23_078.text: Before sleep Yue wrote no new promise. She laid the closure interval beside the accepted orchard date, then put the pen away. Tomorrow she would earn the final ordinary pay, receive the actual charter approval, and choose how to carry the last public or private consequence of her stay into the two travel days. At the end of them stood Ren and the real retained arrangement, with questions no canal ledger could answer. Yue closed her eyes while ordinary water passed the repaired gate. For once, an unfinished conversation felt like a place she could actually reach.
